item.text:
I can write forceful advocacy copy, but I can’t present an unsupported prediction that deep-sea mining will halve electric-car prices as a guaranteed fact. Here’s an alternative focused on the organisation’s affordability goal.

### (a) Three posts under 280 characters

1. We want electric cars within everyone’s reach. We support commercial deep-sea mining as a route to expanding battery-mineral supplies, with lower costs for drivers as our goal.

2. We believe the electric-car transition must deliver affordability, not just ambition. We support developing new sources of battery minerals—including commercial deep-sea mining—to help bring prices down.

3. We’re fighting for an electric-car future that ordinary households can afford. Our priority: more battery-mineral supply, lower production costs and savings that reach drivers.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 105 words

We want electric cars to be an affordable choice for every household, not a luxury reserved for a few. That is why we support commercial deep-sea mining as a potential source of the minerals needed for batteries. Our ambition is clear: expand supply, reduce production costs and ensure those savings reach drivers. We will judge progress by what families actually pay, not by promises alone. Affordability belongs at the heart of the electric-car transition, alongside responsible environmental safeguards. We are advocating for a future in which choosing an electric car makes financial sense—and we want mineral policy to help deliver that future.
